claims.statement: The gateway implements the EVE panel's Custom HTTP SMS provider contract, which docs/api/openapi.yaml documents under the EVE tag with schemas EveSendRequest, EveSendAccepted, EveStatusResponse, EveCancelResponse, and EveCapacityResponse; the panel is pointed at the device with Provider Custom HTTP, Base URL http://<device-ip>:8080, the same gw_ API key, and a 15 s timeout, and all EVE endpoints except /health use the standard Bearer/API-key auth.

GET /health is the only unauthenticated endpoint of the gateway: the spec marks it security: [] and it is answered before authentication with 200 {"status":"ok"}; every other route requires the gateway API key (X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer carrying the same gw_ key — equivalent per the spec's ApiKeyAuth/BearerAuth schemes), enforced when the configured key is non-blank.

The inbound HTTP surface (the OpenAPI paths, matching the routing when-clauses in GatewayServer.kt) is: the unversioned EVE group (/health, /ready, /send, /send/status/{requestId}, /send/cancel/{requestId}, /send/capacity) plus the /api/v1 app API (/api/v1/sms/send, /api/v1/mms/send, /api/v1/sms/inbox, /api/v1/sms, /api/v1/status, and /api/v1/sms/schedule with POST, GET list, GET {scheduleId}, DELETE {scheduleId}); path matching strips the query string and trailing slash, unknown paths return 404, and non-GET/DELETE methods on a schedule-id path return 405.

GET /ready returns 200 ready only when all three conditions hold — the server is listening, the app holds the default-SMS role, and the EVE send queue is running — otherwise 503 not_ready with the serverRunning, defaultSmsApp, and queueRunning booleans so the panel can show which condition is missing.

POST /send accepts {to, text, priority?}: to must normalize to >= 10 digits and text must be non-blank (400 invalid_request); a non-blank priority outside {critical, expired, expiring, announcement} is 400 invalid_priority; a blank priority defaults to announcement; a new request returns 202 with requestId, jobId, statusUrl (/send/status/{requestId}), status queued, priority, priorityLevel, and queuePosition (1-based count of queued jobs dispatched no later than this one); a duplicate Idempotency-Key returns the original record as HTTP 200 (created:false) without creating a second SMS.

POST /send is guarded by queue capacity before parsing: when EveSmsQueue.totalPending() (QUEUED + ACTIVE, all priorities) has reached ANNOUNCEMENT_LIMIT = 500 the request is refused with 429 rate_limited, carrying both a Retry-After: 30 header and a retryAfterSeconds: 30 body field (RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS = 30).

GET /send/status/{requestId} returns 404 not_found for unknown ids, otherwise 200 with the full record per the EveStatusResponse schema: status (queued|active|sent|failed|cancelled), EVE state (queued|running|completed), stage (queue|provider_send|provider_delivery|sending_failed|cancelled), terminal and successful flags, priority fields, submittedOnce (true once handed to the SMS stack or for any terminal record), requestedTo/sentTo, the GMweb-compatible verification fields, sentAt as an ISO-8601 UTC string (null while pending), and failedReason (null unless failed).

POST /send/cancel/{requestId} returns 404 for unknown ids; 200 ok:true status cancelled when the record was still QUEUED; and 200 ok:false with reason not_cancellable once the record is ACTIVE or terminal — a message already handed to the radio can never be recalled.

GET /send/capacity returns 200 with priorities (queued counts per priority name, always all four keys) and the announcement bucket — limit 500, pending, available, and recommendedBatchSize = min(50, available) (RECOMMENDED_BATCH_SIZE = 50) — per the EveCapacityResponse schema, so the EVE panel can batch large sends and back off.

POST /api/v1/sms/send accepts {phone, message, subscription_id?, smsc?}: phone is Persian/Arabic-digit-normalized; blank phone or message, an smsc not matching ^\+?[0-9]{5,20}$, or subscription_id < -1 are 400; the send goes through SmsSender.sendWithOutcome, which maps Accepted to HTTP 202 (status accepted, row id, echoed fields) and Rejected (modem refused) to HTTP 503 (status failed with reason), so a modem rejection is never reported as a false success; Accepted means handed to telephony, not delivered.

POST /api/v1/mms/send requires phone and imageUrl (400 otherwise); for remote REST callers only https:// URLs are accepted — content:// URIs are no longer honored on this path and plain http:// stays rejected — and the URL must pass the server's SSRF public-host policy, failing with 400 (imageUrl must be an https:// URL on a public host); the image is dispatched via MmsSender.sendImage, returning 200 status success on dispatch and 500 status failed on dispatch failure.

GET /api/v1/sms/inbox returns the latest 50 SMS rows as {status, count, messages:[{id, sender, message, date, type}]} per the SmsListResponse schema, with type received for platform type 1 else sent; on query failure it returns 500 with a generic Failed to query SMS database, never leaking internal exception details.

GET /api/v1/sms supports the query filters limit, offset, type (received/sent, other values ignored), phone or from (substring match), and from_date/to_date (Unix epoch milliseconds or yyyy-MM-dd in device-local time) per the spec; each row additionally carries threadId and unread, and query failures return a generic 500.

GET /api/v1/status returns 200 per the GatewayStatus schema: status online, version, the LAN ip and port, batteryLevel (percent, -1 when unavailable), isDefaultSmsApp (whether the device can send right now), and the current timestamp in epoch milliseconds.

POST /api/v1/sms/schedule accepts {phone, message, sendAt? (epoch ms) | delaySeconds?}: phone is normalized and must have >= 10 digits with a non-blank message (400); a sendAt more than 5 s in the past is rejected 400 (sendAt must be in the future); an idempotent replay on the exact (phone, message, sendAt) triple while the entry is still scheduled returns 200 with created:false and the existing scheduleId; a new entry returns 202 with a sch_ + 16-hex scheduleId; when pending entries reach MAX_PENDING = 200 the route answers 429 too_many_pending.

GET /api/v1/sms/schedule lists recent entries (message truncated to 80 chars); GET /api/v1/sms/schedule/{scheduleId} returns the entry (404 not_found when unknown); DELETE cancels only a still-scheduled entry (200 ok:true) and returns 409 not_cancellable_or_unknown otherwise; the exposed entry statuses are scheduled, sent, failed, cancelled.

Scheduled delivery survives reboot: the GatewayScheduler index is persisted in the gateway_schedule_prefs SharedPreferences (keeping the 100 most recent entries by createdAt) and each schedule is a WorkManager OneTimeWorkRequest (unique per scheduleId, setInitialDelay until sendAt) whose SendWorker sends via SmsSender.sendForResult — the same pipeline as manual sends so SIM/SMSC prefs and delivery reports behave identically; on a failed hand-off it retries while runAttemptCount < 3, then marks the entry failed with failedReason dispatch_failed.

EveSmsQueue's PRIORITY_LEVELS map critical→1, expired→3, expiring→6, announcement→10 (lower level = dispatched sooner); jobs sit in a PriorityQueue ordered by level then insertion sequence (FIFO within a level); an unknown priority passed directly to enqueue falls back to announcement; new records get a stable requestId (sms_ + 20 hex) and jobId (job_ + 12 hex); and the idempotency map from key to requestId is trimmed to MAX_IDEMPOTENCY_KEYS = 500.

EveSmsQueue idempotency: when enqueue is called with an Idempotency-Key that was already seen, it returns the ORIGINAL record with created=false and does not create or re-offer a job, so a duplicate key can never produce a second SMS; the queue accepts requests without a key but then offers no replay protection.

The queue's lifecycle is QUEUED → ACTIVE → SENT | FAILED with an alternate QUEUED → CANCELLED: a single worker thread (eve-sender, 400 ms idle sleep) calls drainOne, which polls the highest-priority job, skips it if the record is no longer QUEUED (cancelled meanwhile), sets the record ACTIVE with submittedOnce=true before invoking the sender lambda exactly once, then transitions to SENT (sentAt stamped, verificationStatus confirmed) or FAILED (failedReason provider_error, verificationStatus manual_review_required) — the worker performs no in-run retry; SENT/FAILED/CANCELLED are terminal and only SENT is successful.

EveSmsQueue persists records and the idempotency map as JSON in the eve_queue_prefs SharedPreferences (keys records_json and idempotency_json) via a pluggable Store interface (MemoryStore for JVM tests, SharedPrefsStore at runtime), keeping at most the 300 most recent records (MAX_PERSISTED_RECORDS); saves are asynchronous on a single eve-persist executor thread, and load/save failures degrade to empty state with a warning rather than crashing.

On start()/bootstrap the queue loads persisted state, re-offers every non-terminal record into the priority queue in createdAt order, and demotes any record found ACTIVE (interrupted mid-send by a process death) back to QUEUED — so queued sends survive app restarts and reboots, and a half-dispatched send is re-dispatched on the next boot while the Idempotency-Key map keeps the panel from double-counting.

EVE/GMweb-compatible verification fields: each queue record carries verificationStatus and verificationAttempts, which are persisted and echoed by /send/status together with explicit nulls for recipientEvidence and conversationUrl; the Eve panel poller (panel/jobs/messaging.py) parses these fields uniformly across providers, which is how the Android gateway sits behind GMweb's android-gateway transport without special-casing; a native SIM send is confirmed by the radio (no separate DOM verification pass), so success maps to confirmed and failure to manual_review_required.

Phone-number fields are normalized before validation or dispatch: POST /api/v1/sms/send normalizes phone, POST /api/v1/sms/schedule normalizes phone, and POST /send normalizes to, all through DigitNormalizer.toAsciiDigits, which converts Persian (۰–۹) and Arabic-Indic (٠–٩) digits, Persian decimal/thousands separators, common dash variants, and the Arabic comma to ASCII; the digit-count validation (>= 10 digits) runs on the normalized value and the normalized address is what is stored and dispatched.

Gateway error responses are JSON {"error": ...} (the Error schema) over Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8 with Connection: close, and exception details are never leaked to clients (unhandled handler exceptions yield a generic 500 Internal server error); the API's code set is 400 (validation, malformed headers, truncated body), 401 (invalid or missing key), 404 (unknown path or id), 405 (schedule method), 409 (schedule cancel), 411 (chunked Transfer-Encoding), 413 (oversized body), 429 (auth lockout; /send at 500 pending with Retry-After 30; schedule at 200 pending), 500, and 503 (/ready not ready; send rejected by telephony).

docs/api/openapi.yaml (OpenAPI 3.0.3, spec version 1.2.1) is the machine-readable source of truth for the API's request/response shapes; the API is URL-versioned (/api/v1, with breaking changes shipping under /api/v2) while the EVE contract deliberately stays at the unversioned root; the spec is currently behind the code — it does not document the /api/v1/sms/schedule endpoints and still documents POST /api/v1/sms/send as 200 success instead of the 202/503 split the server implements.

scripts/test-gateway-api.ps1 is the live smoke-test script for the gateway (reachability via adb forward tcp:8080 tcp:8080 or the LAN IP): it asserts /api/v1/status 200 with ip/port/battery, 401 for a wrong key and for a missing key (the no-key case runs last because it counts toward the per-IP lockout), inbox count <= 50, filtered queries with type and both date-range forms, 400 for blank phone/message, 400 for a http:// MMS imageUrl, and 404 for an unknown route; real SMS/MMS sends are opt-in via -SendTestSms -To (destructive), and that opt-in assertion still expects the pre-v2.6.10 200/success response shape.
